messages:
Maria Chen: Heads up — seeing steady memory growth on prod-rt1 during long streaming tool-loop sessions (user sessions >45m). Heap climbs ~800MB over ~30m and does NOT release when session ends. Timeline aligns with KV cache TTL rollover window. Suspect slab / page refs not being reclaimed after eviction/ttl.

Raj Patel: Yikes. Can you paste a heap pprof or allocation top? any hotspots pointing to KV structures?

Maria Chen: Pasted the pprof top from a dump after 30m of sustained long-chat traffic: 
```
(pprof) top10
flat  flat%   sum%        cum  cum%   name
20.1MB 10.2% 10.2%  118.6MB 60.1%  KVPage::alloc
14.8MB 7.5% 17.7%   14.8MB 7.5%   Slab::retain_ref
11.3MB 5.7% 23.4%   11.3MB 5.7%   Chunk::pin
7.2MB 3.6% 27.0%    68.3MB 34.6%  DeferredFreeQueue::enqueue

# note: cumulative shows large retention around KVPage/DeferredFree
```

Sam O'Neill: Those DeferredFreeQueue numbers make me think the deferred free worker isn't draining for some sessions. Maybe it's per-runtime shard keyed by session id and a race leaves pages stuck referenced. Any logs around the eviction worker?

Maria Chen: Attach from prod logs around the TTL rollover window (trimmed):
```
[2026-02-17T09:12:02Z] kv-evict: session=abc123 policy=ttl launched sweep shard=7
[2026-02-17T09:12:02Z] kv-evict: shard7 mark_page page_id=0x7ff1b2e offset=4096 refcnt=1
[2026-02-17T09:12:02Z] kv-evict: shard7 schedule_free page_id=0x7ff1b2e to_deferred_queue
[2026-02-17T09:12:02Z] deferred-free: shard=7 queued page=0x7ff1b2e
[2026-02-17T09:12:02Z] session-toolloop: session=abc123 heartbeat active; pinned_pages=3
[2026-02-17T09:12:02Z] deferred-free: shard=7 worker start drain_count=0
[2026-02-17T09:12:02Z] deferred-free: shard=7 worker delayed (pin detected) page=0x7ff1b2e
[2026-02-17T09:12:02Z] session-toolloop: session ended; pinned_pages->0 but page still in deferred queue
```

Lee Kim: Looks like the worker saw a pinned page and delayed the free. But the page stayed queued after session end. Could be a missing decrement or an orphaned pin that never cleared after session teardown. Any differences between streaming vs non-streaming sessions?

Maria Chen: Yeah, quick comparison: short requests (chat <10m) show deferred-free drain completes within seconds. Long streaming sessions consistently leave 2–5 pages queued per session; we accumulate thousands over hours.

Raj Patel: Two hypotheses: 1) TTL rollover path sets a stale flag but doesn't clear an in-flight session pin if the session holds a weak reference, leaving a dangling strong ref; 2) The deferred-free worker has a backoff loop that can infinite-wait if session heartbeats race in a particular order. I can try to repro locally with a harness that simulates streaming tool loops and heartbeat/teardown alignment.

Sam O'Neill: For repro, this helped earlier: start N sessions, pin pages periodically, then trigger eviction sweep with TTL, and after the session teardown, fast-forward TTL. Code-ish: 
```bash
# simplified repro steps
run-toolloop --sessions 200 --pin-interval 10s --holding-time 45m &
sleep 10s && trigger-evict --force-ttl-rollover
# observe deferred-free queue size via /debug/kv/shard/7/queue
```

Maria Chen: I ran a smaller repro in staging (N=50) and reproduced within ~20m. Attaching sanitized debug dump (link: https://internal/staging/pprof/224789) — gist contains per-shard queue sizes and a small flame graph.

Lee Kim: I instrumented an extra trace in a local build (kv_debug=trace_pin) and got this sequence showing a refcount not being decremented on session teardown: 
```
TRACE shard=7 page=0x7ff1b2e action=pin owner=session:abc123 count=1
TRACE shard=7 page=0x7ff1b2e action=evict mark_stale=true
TRACE shard=7 page=0x7ff1b2e action=deferred_queue enqueue
TRACE shard=7 page=0x7ff1b2e action=unpin owner=session:abc123 count=0  <-- seen
TRACE shard=7 page=0x7ff1b2e action=deferred_worker start drain
TRACE shard=7 page=0x7ff1b2e action=deferred_worker check_pin found 0 but session_ref_missing=true ???
TRACE shard=7 page=0x7ff1b2e action=deferred_worker skip requeue
# page never freed due to session_ref_missing flag, no cleanup path
```

Raj Patel: That session_ref_missing flag path shouldn't prevent final free; it's supposed to fallback to force-free after grace. Looks like a regression from the refactor in commit 1f3b2a9 (deferred-free: add session-weakrefs) — maybe the fallback got removed. Can someone bisect commit range 1f3b2a9..2c7d4e1 on the worker?

Sam O'Neill: I'll start a bisect and run the repro harness in CI. If we can confirm commit, we can roll back or add fix.

Maria Chen: Action items: (1) Sam to run CI bisect + repro (owner: Sam), (2) Raj to add a guard in deferred-free worker to force-free after grace window (owner: Raj), (3) Lee to add extra trace and an automated assertion that deferred queue length drains within Xs after session end (owner: Lee). I'll collect further pprofs and post. Also flagged incident for oncall since prod-rt1 is affected. :warning:

deploy-bot: Incident created INC-2026-0217-KV-ORPHANED-PAGES, severity: high, assigned: eng-runtime-oncall

Raj Patel: One more note — check kernel selection/batching heuristics around deferred-free worker scheduling. If the worker runs on a different scheduling class it might be starved under high batching loads. I'll add a perf counter to track worker latency.

Maria Chen: Thanks team, I'll keep updates here. If anyone hits the repro, paste heap deltas and /debug/kv/shard/*/queue sizes.

Lee Kim: Got a small patch idea to clear session_weakrefs on explicit session destroy; will open PR and link it here.

Sam O'Neill: CI bisect started (job/kv-orphan-bisect/224789). Will post results.
